name: Hanno the Navigator
summary: A Carthaginian fleet sails out past the Pillars of Heracles to found colonies down the Atlantic coast of Africa, then explores further south. The account survives only in a short Greek translation, so how far Hanno got (Senegal, Sierra Leone or Cameroon) is still argued over.

stops.note: Sixty ships carrying colonists set out.
The first colony, beyond the Pillars of Heracles.
A wooded headland, where they build a shrine to Poseidon.
Friendly herders act as interpreters for the voyage south.
An island trading post, as far from the Pillars as Carthage is.
A river full of crocodiles and hippopotamuses: perhaps the Senegal.
At night they see fires and hear pipes and drums from the land.
A great burning mountain: perhaps Mount Kakulima in Guinea, or Mount Cameroon.
They capture three 'hairy people' their guides call gorillai, then turn back for want of supplies.
